meta.scope: Bolivia batch 5 — Remittances as external household support, NBI structural poverty, food insecurity, industrial/manufacturing presence, and FDI. Completes the ~50-candidate depth target.

candidates.title: Remesas familiares / Family remittances
candidates.description: Inflows of personal transfers from Bolivians living abroad. Major secondary-income item in the balance of payments and a direct support to household consumption.
candidates.notes: Lived-economy external support. Annual inflows on the order of USD 1.2–1.3 bn. Spain is the dominant origin (~50%); destination is heavily concentrated in Santa Cruz, Cochabamba and La Paz. Continuously cited as a stabilising source of foreign exchange and household income when other external flows are under pressure.

candidates.title: Necesidades Básicas Insatisfechas (NBI) / Unsatisfied Basic Needs
candidates.description: Structural (non-monetary) poverty measure based on deprivations in housing, services, education and health. Complementary to the income-poverty series.
candidates.notes: Long-run living-conditions indicator. Census-based; shows large historical improvement but a persistent rural–urban gap (rural NBI still several times urban). Housing space and services remain the most frequent deprivations.

candidates.title: Inseguridad alimentaria / Food insecurity (ELCSA scale)
candidates.description: Experience-based food-insecurity indicators from the household survey using the Latin American and Caribbean Food Security Scale.
candidates.notes: Lived hunger and worry indicator. Recent readings show elevated concern about running out of food and a non-trivial share of households reporting hunger; trends have worsened in the early-2020s stress period.

candidates.title: Inversión Extranjera Directa / FDI statistics
candidates.description: Statistics of foreign direct investment flows and stocks by sector. Part of the external accounts and specialised BCB analysis.
candidates.notes: FDI has been modest and concentrated; hydrocarbons and manufacturing have been recurrent destinations. Net flows are small relative to the investment needs implied by the lithium and industrialisation agenda.

candidates.title: Industria manufacturera — producción y exportaciones
candidates.description: Manufacturing production and export statistics. Includes soy derivatives, processed foods, textiles, wood products and other non-traditional manufactures.
candidates.notes: Industrial-commercial layer beyond primary extraction. Soy crushing and related agro-industry dominate the export side; the broader manufacturing base remains relatively shallow.

candidates.title: Empleo formal / Formal employment
candidates.description: Share and absolute number of employed persons in formal jobs (with social-security coverage or registered contracts). Complement to the informality series.
candidates.notes: Protective labour status. Formal workers have substantially lower poverty incidence. The formal share remains a minority of total employment.

candidates.title: Condiciones de vivienda y servicios básicos
candidates.description: Housing quality, overcrowding, and access to water, sanitation and electricity. Core components of the NBI measure and of everyday living standards.
candidates.notes: Direct lived-conditions node. Inadequate housing space is among the most frequent NBI deprivations; rural service gaps remain large.

candidates.title: Mortalidad infantil y neonatal
candidates.description: Infant and neonatal mortality rates. Long-run health-outcome indicator complementary to the maternal-transfer and health-system nodes.
candidates.notes: Long-run improvement is clear (large declines over recent decades), yet levels remain higher than Southern Cone peers. Links to the Juana Azurduy transfer and public-health capacity.

candidates.title: Departamento de Pando — northern Amazonian extreme
candidates.description: Northernmost Amazonian department. Low population density, intermediate poverty, and distinct lowland living conditions.
candidates.notes: Completes the full departmental set. Geographic and demographic extreme relative to the highland and central-axis departments.

candidates.title: Eje central (La Paz – Cochabamba – Santa Cruz)
candidates.description: The three-department demographic and economic corridor that concentrates the majority of population, formal activity, remittance inflows and absolute poverty numbers.
candidates.notes: Analytical geography node. Most remittances, formal jobs and absolute poverty counts sit on this axis; the rest of the country is thinner demographically and economically.

proposed_edges.basis: Remittances are the dominant component of secondary income in the balance of payments.
The large majority of remittance inflows are received in Santa Cruz, Cochabamba and La Paz.
Housing and basic-services deprivations are core components of the NBI measure.
Food-insecurity indicators are derived from the household survey.
Formal and informal employment are complementary partitions of total employment.
Formal employment is strongly associated with lower poverty incidence.
Manufactured and processed goods (especially soy derivatives) form a material non-traditional export line.
FDI flows appear in the financial account of the balance of payments.
Infant-mortality outcomes are a key performance indicator of the health system.
